events.text: Floor {tw_floor}, the Gate of Dust. You have sat in the high councils of heaven, and here you stand in a queue: a farmer with no root, a nervous young climber, a grandmother on a ninth try. The wooden dummy in the room does not know what a god is. It hits you exactly as hard as it hit the grandmother, and you beat it the way anyone must: with the basics.

choices.text: Wait your turn behind the grandmother next time

effects.log: The grandmother tells you to keep your elbow in. You keep it in. It helps.

choices.text: Ask the dummy why it does not kneel

effects.log: It does not answer. It is a dummy. The farmer behind you laughs until they have to sit down.

choices.text: Strike it once with the whole weight of your godhood

effects.log: The blow lands like any other. The Tower does not count what you are, only what you do. The dummy rocks, and rocks back.

events.text: The dummy on floor {tw_floor} strikes harder every time you hold back, and a god of battle has never had to hold anything back. You hit it with a sliver of what you are, then with more, and the more you use the harder it answers. In the end it knocks you down the stairs into the dust, in front of a dozen mortals who saw everything.

choices.text: Get up and bow to the dummy

effects.log: You bow. A child in the queue bows too, copying you. The dust settles on both of you the same.

choices.text: Brush off the dust and say nothing

effects.log: Nobody in heaven will hear of this, you tell yourself. Within the year a comic song about it has reached the golden roads.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is a floor of dust that fills again as fast as you sweep it. The climbers ahead of you blasted it with qi and are still here, coughing. Your domain is the kind that makes things grow, and growing is never hurried: you sweep a little, and wait, and sweep a little more, the way a field is tended. On the hundredth stroke the dust stays down.

choices.text: Show the coughing climbers how

effects.log: You hand one of them the broom. It takes them most of the year. They thank you without ever learning your name.

choices.text: Go on up alone

effects.log: You climb. Behind you the dust begins to rise again for the next climber, which you suppose is the point.

events.text: You carry your pantheon's banner up the stairs of floor {tw_floor}, because the order said to plant it at the top. The Tower lets you through, banner and all. But it grows heavier with every step, as if it were woven from every climber it has ever been carried past, and by the landing you are bent under it like a porter.

choices.text: Keep carrying it

effects.log: You carry it. Your shoulders ache by the end of the year. The banner does not care.

choices.text: Roll it up and tie it to your back

effects.log: Rolled up, it weighs the same. The Tower is not interested in how you carry your pride.

choices.text: Lean it against the wall and leave it

effects.log: You leave it standing on the landing. It looks smaller there. One day, coming down, you will have to explain.

events.text: Halfway up floor {tw_floor}, something reaches you that should not reach anyone inside the Tower: a prayer. Then another. The people of {pw_world} are praying to their god, and their words have found you here in the dust, small and far away. The mortal beside you hears nothing. You hear them ask for rain, and a safe birth, and, one of them, for their god to be well.

choices.text: Answer them, even from here

effects.log: You send a little of yourself the long way down to {pw_world}. It rains there. Here the next step is harder, as if the Tower noticed what you spent.

choices.text: Keep the prayers and climb on

effects.log: You keep them in your sleeve like letters to read later. They are warm all year.

events.text: You fell on floor {tw_floor}, a god on the Gate of Dust, and rolled all the way down to the first step. The Keeper does not stand up. They pour a second cup of barley tea, in the same chipped cup they give everyone, and push it along the step toward you. "Most gods fall about here," they say. "The ones who come back are worth the tea."

choices.text: Drink the tea

effects.log: It is cold, and plain, and the best thing you have tasted in a thousand years.

choices.text: Ask how many gods have come back

effects.log: "Enough to count," says the Keeper, "and not enough to stop counting." They go back to sweeping.

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} a family of mortal climbers recognises you from the shrine in their village. They kneel on the dusty boards in the middle of the climb, and the queue behind them stops. The Keeper calls up the stairwell without looking: "Nobody kneels in here. It blocks the stairs." Everyone turns to see what a god does now.

choices.text: Kneel beside them, then help them up

effects.log: You kneel too, which frightens them more than anything. Then you help them up, and the queue moves again.

choices.text: Tell them to get up and climb

effects.log: "Climb," you say, and they do. In here, it turns out, that is the best blessing you have.

choices.text: Step out of the queue and let them go first

effects.log: You go to the back. A god at the back of the line is a strange sight. The Keeper, below, says "Hm."

events.text: In the Hall of Echoes the banner on your back begins to speak in the voices of gods who once carried it here. Every one of them reached this floor or the next, and went home. "Plant it here," they say. "This is far enough to call a conquest." Floor {tw_floor} waits, and the pole is warm, as if hands had only just let go of it.

choices.text: Plant it here, as they did

effects.log: The pole will not stand in the lacquered floor. It falls and rolls, and the echoes go quiet. They never planted it either. They only said they had.

choices.text: Climb on with it, past the floor where they stopped

effects.log: You climb past the floor where every one of them turned back. The banner goes light at once. It was never the banner that was heavy.

choices.text: Give the banner to the echoes and keep climbing

effects.log: The echoes take it the way the dead take things: gently, and for good. Your pantheon will ask. You will have to tell the truth.

events.text: The echo on floor {tw_floor} wears a crown of a shape no god wears any more. It was a god of an age before the pantheons, and it climbed this far, and stopped, and its echo has waited here ever since. It fights well. It loses to you. Afterwards it asks, politely, whether its temples still stand. You have never heard its name.

choices.text: Tell it the truth

effects.log: It nods. "Then I was only a god," it says, and seems relieved. It points out a loose step it never fixed.

choices.text: Ask its name, and promise to remember it

effects.log: It tells you. It is a long name, and you carry it up with you. Somewhere, you suppose, that counts as a temple.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is full of the echoes of mortals who prayed to your domain: people who asked for one more year, one good dream, a kinder thread. You answered some of them. Here they stand in a row and fight you one after another. None of them are angry. They only want to see what their god is like up close.

choices.text: Speak with each of them before you go

effects.log: It takes the year. Each echo bows when you finish. The last one says, "You are smaller than we thought. That is good."

choices.text: Ask the ones you never answered why they still came

effects.log: "Who else would we ask?" says one. You have no answer, and you carry the lack of one up the stairs.

events.text: The echo that beats you on floor {tw_floor} did not come from your side of the Tower. It is a deity of the other sky, tall, with a lantern on a long pole, who climbed up through the western gate in some age you never knew: Maelis of the Long Lantern. It fights with light and a quiet rite, and it is very good. Standing over you it looks puzzled. "You are a god too? Then you know. It does not help in here."

choices.text: Ask how far it climbed

effects.log: "Far enough to stop being a goddess," says Maelis, "and not far enough to be anything else." It helps you up, and is gone.

choices.text: Ask for a rematch next year

effects.log: The echo laughs, a sound like a bell in a stone hall. "Echoes do not keep appointments," it says. "Climbers do."

events.text: Two echoes are already fighting on floor {tw_floor} when you arrive: gods of two pantheons, from a war in heaven older than your godhood. They stopped mid-blow, and the Tower kept them. One wears your pantheon's colours. It sees you and shouts for help. The other only looks tired.

choices.text: Help the echo of your pantheon

effects.log: The two of you drive the other echo back. Your ally laughs and thanks you, and you feel nothing at all, because neither of them is real any more.

choices.text: Step between them

effects.log: Both blows stop a finger's width from you. The echoes look at each other properly for the first time in an age, and lower their arms.

choices.text: Walk past both

effects.log: You leave them to it. The war in heaven was never yours to finish, and certainly not in here.

events.text: The bronze mirror on floor {tw_floor} will not show you as a god. It shows the mortal you were at the start of this life, before the first breath of qi: thinner, hungrier, afraid of winter. That face looks out at you across the ages and asks, without words, whether all of this was worth what it cost.

choices.text: Nod to it

effects.log: The mortal in the bronze nods back, and smiles, and the mirror is only bronze.

choices.text: Tell it about the gods

effects.log: You tell it everything. It listens open-mouthed, the way you would have. When you finish it asks if you are happy, and you have to think.

events.text: The mirror on floor {tw_floor} shows {pw_world}, and in its temples a god being worshipped. It wears your face. It is not you. The false god turns in the bronze, looks straight out at you, and smiles, and you lose the floor in the moment it takes you to understand that it is wearing what your people gave you.

choices.text: Swear to take back your temples

effects.log: You swear it to the bronze. The false god only smiles wider. It knows you are here, and not there.

choices.text: Look away from the mirror

effects.log: You look at the floor instead. Some things are better faced at home. It is still there when you close your eyes.

events.text: The mirror of floor {tw_floor} shows your seat in your pantheon's hall, and the gods around it, talking about you while you are away. Nothing they say is cruel. All of it is about what you are for: a domain held, a front kept, a vote. Not one of them says your name. They say your use.

choices.text: Remember every word, and serve them anyway

effects.log: Loyalty with open eyes is still loyalty. You climb on, quieter.

choices.text: Decide to be more than your use to them

effects.log: Nothing changes in the mirror. Something changes in you, and your pantheon will notice it in time.

choices.text: Break the mirror

effects.log: The bronze cracks across your empty seat. The Tower does not punish you. It simply sets out a new mirror next year.

events.text: The mirror on floor {tw_floor} shows the battles fought in your name: banners with your sign on them, soldiers who shouted your domain as they charged. You never lifted a hand in most of them. You did not have to. The bronze shows the faces of the ones who did, one by one, until you have looked at them all.

choices.text: Look at every face to the end

effects.log: It takes the year. When the mirror goes dark you know a little better what your domain costs the people who pray to it.

choices.text: Turn the mirror to the wall

effects.log: The bronze is heavy and the floor is patient. You win the floor and lose the faces. Some of them come back at night.

events.text: You fall from floor {tw_floor} and land, as everyone does, at the first step. The Keeper sets down the broom. "Gods fall the same distance as everyone," they say. "They only land harder, because they are not used to it." They offer you a hand, the same hand they offer the mortals. It is rough from the broom.

choices.text: Take the hand

effects.log: You take it. The Keeper pulls you up with surprising strength. "Again next year," they say.

choices.text: Get up on your own

effects.log: You get up on your own. The Keeper nods, as if that, too, were a perfectly good answer.

events.text: The beasts of floor {tw_floor} know their god. When the cages open they do not come out fighting; they come out and lie down, and the floor will not let you pass while they do, because nothing up here is given for what you are. So you open the cages wider and tell them, as their god, to fight you properly. They do. It is the best fight of your life.

choices.text: Thank each of them by name

effects.log: You know every one of their names. They go back into the cages of their own accord, and one of them licks your hand.

choices.text: Leave every cage open behind you

effects.log: The Keeper mentions, much later, that the beasts of that floor now come and go as they like. "They seem happier," the Keeper says. "The floor is harder. Good."

events.text: A pack of iron-grey hounds and a single bowl of grain wait on floor {tw_floor}. You beat the pack. Afterwards they sit around the bowl and do not touch it, because there is not enough. Your domain is the kind where there is always enough. Here you have only the one bowl.

choices.text: Divide the grain into fair handfuls

effects.log: There is enough, just, when nobody takes more than a handful. The hounds eat. You take nothing.

choices.text: Give the bowl to the smallest hound

effects.log: The others let it eat first. They seem to have been waiting for someone to decide.

events.text: The serpent in the iron pool of floor {tw_floor} answered to your domain once, long ago, in open water, before anyone thought to cage it. You call it the way a god calls weather. It does not come. It rises in its own time, beats you, and sinks again, as if to say that a cage is a cage and a god is only a climber here.

choices.text: Sit by the pool until it rises again

effects.log: It rises after a month and looks at you. You do not call it. That, it seems, was right. Next time it will remember.

choices.text: Go down and come back stronger

effects.log: You go down the stairs with water in your sleeves. You will not call it again. You will climb past it.

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} a young climber in the plain clothes of {pw_people} is fighting a caged boar and losing. You know the stitching of those clothes; you made the world they were sewn in. The climber has come all the way from {pw_world} to the Tower, which stands in every world at once, and does not know that their god is on the same stair.

choices.text: Help them, without saying who you are

effects.log: You drive the boar back. They thank you as one climber thanks another and say their name is Ulla. You keep the name.

choices.text: Watch, and let them win it themselves

effects.log: They win, barely, and sit down on the stair shaking. They never see you. You are prouder than you have been in a century.

events.text: The Scales of floor {tw_floor} do not weigh you. They weigh what you carry. On one pan the Tower sets the prayers of {pw_world}, this year's worship, bright as coins. On the other it sets nothing at all. "Spend it," the floor seems to say. "A god may buy a floor with worship. Gods often have." The pans tremble, waiting for your hand.

choices.text: Spend the worship to tip the scale

effects.log: The worship pours onto the pan and the stair opens at once. You climb it. It feels like climbing on other people's shoulders, because it is.

choices.text: Take the prayers back off the scale

effects.log: You lift them off one by one and climb with only what you are. The floor lets you pass anyway. The Scales, it seems, were weighing whether you would spend them.

choices.text: Send the worship home as a blessing

effects.log: You turn the bright pile around and send it back to {pw_world} as a good harvest. The Scales hold perfectly still. You have the odd feeling they approve.

events.text: On the jade landing of floor {tw_floor} a climber passes you going up, wrapped in borrowed light. You know that light. It is the worship of {pw_world}, the share the false god stole from you, and the false god is wearing it like a cloak to climb the Tower. The Scales do not weigh it at all. It is not here, the floor seems to say. It never earned a step.

choices.text: Follow it up

effects.log: You climb after it. The borrowed light leaves a trail on the stair, easy to follow and very cold.

choices.text: Let it climb, and tend your world

effects.log: You let it go. A thief climbing on stolen prayers will meet a floor that weighs it. You turn your thoughts to the temples of {pw_world} instead.

events.arc: The False God on the Stairs

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} the jade pans hold your pantheon's order to seize the Tower, which you refused, and the loyalty you lost by refusing it. The scale does not tip either way. "Most gods who come here carried the order up," the floor seems to say. "You are the first in a long while who carried it back."

choices.text: Ask what the scale is weighing

effects.log: Nothing, you realise. It is only holding still, which on this floor is a kind of praise.

choices.text: Leave your lost loyalty on the pan

effects.log: You leave it there. Whatever your pantheon thinks it lost, the Tower is keeping it safe.

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} the scales hold one stranger's life: a thread, a ferry token, a dream, whatever your domain would see in it. The floor asks you to weigh it. As a god you could read the whole of it at a glance. The Scales ask you to weigh it the way a mortal judge must, without knowing how it ends.

choices.text: Weigh it blind

effects.log: You close your divine sight and weigh what you can see: a tired face, a kind hand. The scale settles. You were nearly right.

choices.text: Read the whole life first

effects.log: You read it all. The scale tips, then tips back. Knowing everything, it turns out, does not make you fair.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} asks for a choice you must make alone, and you are not used to being alone. Out of habit you reach for the strength of your worshippers, and the jade floor turns it away like a coin it does not take. The pans swing against you. Your own weight, the Scales seem to say. Not theirs.

choices.text: Try again next year, with only yourself

effects.log: You go down the stairs lighter than you came up, and not in the way you wanted.

choices.text: Ask the Keeper whether gods ever pass the Scales

effects.log: "Some," says the Keeper. "The ones who forget to be gods for a floor or two." They hand you the broom for a while.

events.text: Ulla of {pw_world} is a floor ahead of you on the silver shelves of the Past. You find out because the scroll of floor {tw_floor} has two names on it today, theirs and yours, and theirs is first. On the landing they are reading their own past lives. One of them, they tell you, was a farmer who prayed to their god every morning and was never once answered.

choices.text: Tell Ulla who you are

effects.log: Ulla looks at you for a long time. "Then why did you not answer?" they ask. You tell the truth: you did not hear. You were busy being a god.

choices.text: Say only that gods are busier than they should be

effects.log: Ulla shrugs. "Then we pray for them too," they say. You climb past, and your ears burn for a floor.

events.text: Among the silver scrolls of floor {tw_floor} you find the climbs of gods. There is a whole shelf. On it is your pantheon's eldest god: a climb of eleven floors, ten thousand years ago, ending on a broken step. In your pantheon's hall that god tells everyone the Tower was beneath them. The scroll says they wept on the stair.

choices.text: Put the scroll back and keep the secret

effects.log: You put it back exactly where it was. Some day you may need to be kind to that god. Now you know how.

choices.text: Copy it to take home

effects.log: You copy it in your own hand. You do not yet know what you will do with it, which is the most dangerous kind of knowing.

choices.text: Find your own scroll

effects.log: Yours is on the same shelf, newer, still being written. It is already longer than eleven floors. You climb on.

events.text: The past self on floor {tw_floor} comes from this very life: you, above the clouds, the year before you became a god. It is proud, and tired, and sure that godhood will at last be enough. You win. It looks at what you are now and asks, very quietly, whether it was.

choices.text: Tell it no

effects.log: It nods slowly, as if it had suspected. "Then why are you climbing?" it asks. You climb, which is your answer.

choices.text: Tell it yes, and mean it

effects.log: It does not believe you, and is glad you said it anyway. It steps aside.

choices.text: Tell it the climbing was what was missing

effects.log: It considers this the way you would. "Then climb faster," it says. You do.

events.text: A god of a rival pantheon followed you into the Tower to settle a grudge from heaven, and found out on floor {tw_floor} what you are finding out too: in here, neither of you is a god. The silver floor sets you both against your own past selves at once, and you lose to yours while watching theirs. Your rival, panting on the next shelf, laughs at you, and then at the whole war.

choices.text: Call a truce for as long as the Tower lasts

effects.log: The rival thinks about it and holds out a hand. Above the clouds your pantheons are at each other's throats. In here the two of you share a ration.

choices.text: Promise to settle it at the top

effects.log: "At the top," the rival agrees, and you both know neither of you may get there. It is a better promise than most gods make.

events.text: The array of floor {tw_floor} has been redrawn by someone who climbed ahead of you. Where the gold lines should lead up, they lead back into {pw_world}: into an old temple of yours, where your people are being told their god has abandoned them for a tower. The false god left this for you, a trap made of your own worship. You solve it. It still hurts.

choices.text: Redraw the lines toward the stair

effects.log: You draw them back the way the Tower meant. In the temple of the array, a priest stops in the middle of a sentence and looks up.

choices.text: Speak to the people in the array

effects.log: You tell them you have not left. Inside the array, at least, they hear you. Whether it reaches the real temple you cannot know.

events.arc: The False God on the Stairs

events.text: The array of floor {tw_floor} is drawn to put out divinity. The moment you step into it your domain goes dark, the prayers stop, and the long weight of godhood falls off you like a cloak. You are only what you were before. You try to solve the array with a power you no longer have, and it folds the room around you.

choices.text: Learn to stand in the dark

effects.log: You sit inside the dead array until the year ends, learning to think without being a god. Next time you will start there.

choices.text: Go down and rage at the Keeper

effects.log: The Keeper listens to all of it, sweeping. "It is the same array for everyone," they say. "Most people never had a domain to lose."

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} puts out your divinity the moment you enter, as it does every god. You expected it. For a whole year you solve its gold array with nothing but what you learned before godhood: patience, a little arithmetic, the habit of looking at the stone everyone else steps over. When it opens, your domain comes back, and for a moment it feels like a borrowed coat.

choices.text: Shrug it back on

effects.log: It fits. It always will. But you know now where it ends and you begin.

choices.text: Leave it off for a floor

effects.log: You climb the next stair as no god at all. The air is colder. Your feet are more your own.

events.text: Half of the array on floor {tw_floor} is written in letters no scholar of heaven can read, and halfway through the year you find someone solving that half from the other side: a deity of the other sky named Oswin of the Ninefold Ward, frowning at your half as you frown at theirs. Neither of you can rule this floor. You can only finish it together.

choices.text: Solve it side by side

effects.log: You trade lines across the array without a shared tongue. When it opens, Oswin bows the way their people do, a hand on the heart, and goes back down the western stair.

choices.text: Race Oswin to the answer

effects.log: You finish first, by a breath. Oswin laughs and says something that is plainly a compliment, and a little rude.

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} the Dao of the room is one you planted in {pw_world} when you made it, and Ulla understands it better than you do. They grew up inside it. You only made it. In the Tower that is not the same thing. On the landing Ulla looks up at the stairs and says they are going home: they climbed this far to see their god, and now they have.

choices.text: Ask Ulla to go on climbing

effects.log: Ulla shakes their head and smiles. "Someone has to tell them what you are like," they say, and go down. {pw_world} will have a new story by spring.

choices.text: Bless the road home

effects.log: You bless it as a god, and Ulla laughs, because no blessing works inside the Tower. "It is the thought," they say, and go.

choices.text: Let them go, and climb on alone

effects.log: You climb on alone. A child of your world went higher than most gods. You do not need the Tower to tell you what that means.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is the Dao your own domain is made of, turned into a room. In heaven it answers to you. Here it does not know you are its god. It treats you as it would a clever student who has read a great deal and touched very little, and asks you a question about itself that you cannot answer.

choices.text: Admit you do not know

effects.log: The room seems pleased. It answers its own question, slowly, and you understand your domain a little better than you did when you ruled it.

choices.text: Answer as a god would

effects.log: You answer grandly. The room lets you pass the way a teacher lets a proud student pass: with a note in the margin.

events.text: A herald of your pantheon has climbed seventy floors to find you, which is more than most gods have done, and reaches floor {tw_floor} out of breath and furious with the stairs. The order is simple: you are higher than any of your pantheon has ever been, so hold this floor for them. Bar the stair. The Tower has no opinion at all.

choices.text: Bar the stair in your pantheon's name

effects.log: You stand across the stair. A mortal climber walks through you as if you were mist, and on up. The herald writes it down, white-faced.

choices.text: Refuse: the Tower is no one's to hold

effects.log: The herald stares, then begins the long climb down. In heaven, by the end of the year, it is a scandal.

choices.text: Teach the herald to climb

effects.log: You show the herald how. They reach one floor higher than any herald ever has, and go home quieter.

events.text: On floor {tw_floor} the white jade goes silent mid-word, and you feel it: Heaven, listening. Not to the mortals below. To you. Gods speak to Heaven often, and Heaven rarely answers. Here it does not answer either. It only listens, the way a stranger listens on a road, uncertain, waiting to hear what you will say when nobody is bound to obey you.

choices.text: Say nothing at all

effects.log: The silence holds a long time. Somewhere above, something that does not know what it wants seems a little less alone.

choices.text: Ask Heaven what it wants

effects.log: No answer comes. But for one breath the floor feels like a held breath, as if no god had ever asked before.

choices.text: Tell Heaven what you want

effects.log: You say it plainly. You are surprised how small it is. The silence keeps it.

events.text: You lose floor {tw_floor} to a Dao you thought you had mastered, which is the worst way to lose. Your godhood stands on it; in heaven you are its master. Here it went on without you, wider than you, and when you came down the stairs you were not sure, for a whole season, which of you had been holding the other up.

choices.text: Study it again from the beginning

effects.log: You start again, as a student. It is humiliating, and it is the best year of study you have had in a thousand.

choices.text: Go home to your domain and heal

effects.log: You go home and let your domain hold you. It still does. It just did not, up there.

events.text: In the Storm of floor {tw_floor} the false god has stopped. The tribulation found the borrowed light and stripped it off bolt by bolt, and what is left underneath is small and grey and very frightened: a thing that wanted to be loved and never learned how to earn it. It watches you climb past. It asks whether you will tell your people what it looked like.

choices.text: Tell it you will tell them the truth

effects.log: It shrinks a little more, and nods. The truth, it seems, was the only thing it had not stolen.

choices.text: Offer it a hand up

effects.log: It stares at your hand as if it had never seen one. Then it takes it, climbs one floor beside you, and is gone in the next bolt.

choices.text: Leave it to the storm

effects.log: You climb on. Behind you the storm keeps working. Whatever comes down from it will be smaller still.

events.arc: The False God on the Stairs

events.text: A war in heaven spills into the Tower on floor {tw_floor}. The storm is not the Tower's alone: it is the weather of two pantheons, carried up the stairs by gods who could not leave their quarrel at the gate. Their thunder and their banners tear through the tribulation meant for you, and the lightning finds you in the middle of both.

choices.text: Shout for both sides to stop

effects.log: Nobody hears you over the storm. But some of them see you, a god on the stair caught in their war, and one or two go home.

choices.text: Fight your way down through it

effects.log: You go down through the gods' weather and come out scorched and furious. The war will end. The Tower will still be here.

events.text: The tribulation of floor {tw_floor} is made of your own domain. The thunder, the wind, the weight that answers you in heaven comes down on you as if it had never heard your name. It does not refuse you in anger. It refuses you because, for one floor, it is free. You stand in it until the last bolt, and it lets you through.

choices.text: Bow to your own domain

effects.log: You bow to the storm. It seems surprised. At home your domain answers you a little more gently, as if you had both learned something.

choices.text: Command it, just once, to see

effects.log: It ignores you entirely. You laugh in the rain like a mortal, and climb.

events.text: The storm of floor {tw_floor} offers mercy, as the Storm offers everyone: kneel, and the lightning will pass over. Gods do not kneel; it is nearly the first thing a god learns. You stood the whole tribulation through and you are still standing. The offer stays open on the last cloud anyway, as if the storm wanted to see what a god does when kneeling would cost nothing.

choices.text: Kneel, now that nobody needs you to

effects.log: You kneel on the cloud. No lightning comes. Nobody sees it but the storm, and the storm keeps secrets.

choices.text: Stay standing

effects.log: You stay standing. The storm grumbles away. You are not sure you won that one.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is silent, and for the first time since you became a god, so are the prayers. Not one reaches you. {pw_world} has not forgotten you; the Silence simply lets nothing in. You did not know how much of you was made of being asked for things. You sit in the mist and find out what is left.

choices.text: Sit until you know

effects.log: It takes the whole year. What is left is smaller than a god and larger than you feared. The stairs appear.

choices.text: Pray yourself, to no one

effects.log: You have never prayed. You do it badly, the way your people did at first. Nobody answers. You feel better anyway.

events.text: At the door to floor {tw_floor} there is a peg, and on the peg hang crowns: dozens of them, old, dusty, some still faintly bright. Gods hung them here and went on up, and not one came back for theirs. The mist waits. Your own divinity sits on you like a hat you forgot you were wearing.

choices.text: Hang yours on the peg

effects.log: You hang it beside the others. The mist parts at once. Below, very far, a broom stops for a breath.

choices.text: Keep it and walk on

effects.log: You keep it. The Silence does not mind. It is only that the crown weighs more here than anywhere else.

events.text: Floor {tw_floor} is mist, and in the mist sits a deity of the other sky, crowned in grey stone, who climbed up through the western gate in some age before yours and stopped here. It does not speak; nothing speaks in the Silence. It only lifts one hand, as one god greets another. You lose the floor sitting beside it, because for a whole year you cannot think why either of you came.

choices.text: Lift a hand back

effects.log: You lift a hand. Somewhere beyond the mist, where the two gates meet, someone else is still climbing.

choices.text: Stand up and leave it there

effects.log: You stand. It does not follow. Even gods stop somewhere. You would rather not stop here.
